This suggests a potential mechanistic pathway involving the treatment of Kaposi's Sarcoma with doxorubicin, which may influence the development or progression of mature B-cell neoplasms. The evidence implies a possible role of doxorubicin in modulating immune responses or cellular processes that are dysregulated in B-cell malignancies, though the exact mechanism remains unclear. The clinical link between doxorubicin and Kaposi's Sarcoma, along with its association with B-cell neoplasms, supports the hypothesis that it may exert a therapeutic effect on these conditions, though further investigation is needed to elucidate the precise biological mechanisms at play.
